page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8269CY processor based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 vCPUs mapped across 16 dedicated physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, paired with 256.0 GB of system memory. This configuration provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage and standard graphics output, while baseline network throughput is rated at 6 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent multi-threaded capabilities balanced against modest single-core throughput. In Geekbench testing, the server recorded a single-core score of 945.0 alongside a multi-core score of 8252.0. Similarly, stress-ng recorded 1108.09 on single-core testing and 23524.55 in multi-threaded execution. PassMark yielded an overall CPU score of 23224.93 and a memory score of 1876.15. For memory operations, uncached large-block read bandwidth reached 98.84 GB/sec and write bandwidth achieved 48.76 GB/sec. In application-focused benchmarks, Redis SET operations reached 22.17 million operations per second, and database operations achieved a PassMark score of 8599.55.

Hardware efficiency stems from its massive memory allocation relative to compute capacity, making it cost-efficient for tasks demanding large working datasets without requiring excessive vCPU scaling. However, workloads requiring intensive per-thread compute or fast integrated NVMe storage face architectural tradeoffs due to lower single-core benchmark percentiles and reliance on remote block storage.

The ecs.se1.8xlarge is suited for in-memory databases like Redis or Memcached, large-scale enterprise database hosting, distributed caching layers, and high-memory analytics processing that benefit from 256 GB of dedicated RAM.
